## 1. Purpose / Scope

This CRB submission seeks conceptual approval for the **Platform Gainwell Inbound File Scanning Service** — a platform security capability that intercepts, scans, and dispositions all inbound file streams before they reach any destination storage volume (S3 buckets, EFS, databases, and API-connected volumes) across Platform Gainwell. The following concerns are addressed:

1. ✅ **Clearly define business problem**: Platform Gainwell currently has no platform-wide control mandating malware or virus scanning of inbound file streams before they reach destination storage. Files submitted by external partners and internal systems traverse from ingest channel to destination without any antivirus inspection at the platform layer. This gap creates material risk that ransomware, trojans, and weaponized documents delivered via B2B file exchange, internal application uploads, or API submissions will infiltrate Medicaid and healthcare data stores that contain PHI.
2. ✅ **Ensure strategic alignment**: Directly supports Gainwell's security-first cloud platform posture and HIPAA §164.308(a)(1) mandate to identify and protect against reasonably anticipated threats to PHI. The capability closes a documented gap in the Cloud and Infrastructure Security domain capability map (GUID-SEC-CLOUD-CAP-MAP-0.6.02) and is required by NIST 800-53 SI-3 (Malicious Code Protection).
3. ✅ **Identify key stakeholders**: Platform Engineering (implementation ownership), Security Operations Center (SOC alert consumer and incident responder), Enterprise Architecture Practice (governance and ABB ownership), Application/Integration teams operating ingest channels (integration consumers), Compliance & Privacy (HIPAA and FedRAMP audit evidence).
4. ✅ **Provide conceptual architecture**: Fail-closed staging/landing zone intercept model — files land in a transient staging store, are scanned by a containerized antivirus engine, tagged with a structured scan result, and either promoted to their destination or quarantined with real-time SOC notification. Three ingest channel patterns are covered in v1: AWS Transfer Family (SFTP), S3 direct PUT, and API Gateway file uploads.
5. ✅ **Assess preliminary risks**: Definition staleness on pipeline failure, Lambda cold start latency against Transfer Family throughput SLA, quarantine store access misconfiguration, zip bomb / nested archive attacks, and PHI classification inheritance across scan tiers — all with defined mitigation strategies.
6. ✅ **Consider regulatory and compliance**: HIPAA §164.308(a)(1), NIST 800-53 SI-3 (Malicious Code Protection), SI-3(2) (Automatic Updates), IR-6 (Incident Reporting), and AU-9 (Protection of Audit Information) are directly addressed by the capability design.
7. ✅ **Estimate costs and timeline**: Estimated Phase 1 implementation in two sprints (~4 weeks); AWS service cost baseline ~$261/month at 100GB ingest volume (per AWS Solutions Library reference). Cost scales with ingest volume on a serverless consumption model.
8. ✅ **Evaluate alternatives**: Three scan engine approaches have been identified for evaluation — ClamAV on Lambda (open-source, AWS Solutions Library validated), Amazon GuardDuty Malware Protection for S3 (AWS-native managed service), and commercial AV SDK on Lambda. Engine selection is governed by **ADR-SEC-003-FILE-SCAN**, currently under Security Architecture review, and is intentionally decoupled from this CRB. The conceptual capability and surrounding platform pattern are engine-agnostic and are not dependent on the ADR outcome.

## 3. Executive Summary

**Project Overview**: The Platform Gainwell Inbound File Scanning Service establishes an ingest-boundary antivirus and malware scanning capability across all file upload paths into Platform Gainwell. Every inbound file is held in a transient staging store and scanned for malware before any promotion to a destination volume. Infected files are quarantined and the Security Operations Center is alerted in real time. The capability enforces a fail-closed posture and automates daily virus definition updates. The foundational architecture pattern is derived from the AWS Solutions Library guidance for malware detection using AWS Transfer Family Managed Workflows.

**Business Problem**: Platform Gainwell handles Protected Health Information (PHI) and Personally Identifiable Information (PII) for state Medicaid programs across multiple ingest channels. Currently, no platform-wide control scans inbound files for malware before they reach destination S3 buckets, databases, or other storage systems. External partners submit files via SFTP (AWS Transfer Family), internal applications write directly to S3, and portal users upload documents via API. Any of these channels can be the vector for malicious content — ransomware, trojans, or weaponized documents — that, if successfully ingested, could compromise PHI stores, trigger a HIPAA breach notification, or cause downstream data system disruption. The absence of ingest-boundary scanning is a documented gap in the Cloud and Infrastructure Security capability model.

**Stakeholder Impact**: Platform Engineering gains a reusable, infrastructure-as-code provisioned scanning service deployable across all ingest channels without per-channel custom security logic. The Security Operations Center gains real-time, structured alert notification on every malicious file detection with full context (source channel, threat name, uploader identity, object reference). Application and integration teams owning ingest channels are required to route file uploads through the scanning workflow — the integration contract is defined by the Inbound File Scanning ABB (GUID-SEC-CLOUD-FILE-SCAN-2.6.11) and is designed to minimize the integration burden on channel owners. The compliance function gains an auditable scan record for every inbound file, supporting HIPAA audit evidence for SI-3 compliance.

### Business Value

- **Risk Reduction**: Directly mitigates the risk of malicious content infiltrating PHI stores via ingest channels. A successful ransomware ingest into a Medicaid data environment carries potential financial, regulatory, and reputational impact well in excess of the cost of the scanning service.
- **Compliance**: Closes the NIST 800-53 SI-3 gap in Platform Gainwell's cloud security posture. Provides automated, auditable evidence of malicious code protection at information system entry points as required by HIPAA §164.308(a)(1).
- **Operational Efficiency**: Centralizes ingest security logic at the platform layer. Individual application and integration teams are relieved of implementing per-channel antivirus logic independently. A single platform-managed service protects all channels uniformly.
- **SOC Effectiveness**: Structured real-time alerting provides the SOC with actionable, contextualized notification on every INFECTED event — replacing the current state of no automated detection with a measurable detection-to-alert pipeline.

### Business Process Workflow

**Current State**: Files submitted to Platform Gainwell via SFTP (Transfer Family), S3 direct PUT, or API upload travel from the ingest channel directly to a destination S3 bucket, EFS mount, or database store without any antivirus inspection at the platform layer. There is no automated detection of malicious content at the ingest boundary. The SOC has no visibility into malicious file submissions unless a downstream system or endpoint agent detects post-ingest activity.

**Future State**: All inbound files land in a transient staging bucket (landing zone). An automated workflow triggers the ClamAV scan Lambda on each file. Files confirmed CLEAN are promoted to the destination store. Files detected as INFECTED are moved to an isolated quarantine store — inaccessible to downstream systems — and a structured SOC alert is dispatched within a 5-minute SLO. All scan outcomes (CLEAN and INFECTED) are recorded to an immutable audit log. Virus definitions refresh automatically daily via an EventBridge Scheduler → CodeBuild → ECR pipeline.

### Conceptual Architecture Overview

The service spans four logical layers:

**Layer 1 — Staging / Landing Zone**
A transient S3 bucket (landing zone) that acts as the mandatory security checkpoint for all inbound files. No ingest channel holds write access to any destination store directly. All inbound files land here first. Object expiry policy prevents indefinite accumulation.

**Layer 2 — Scan Workflow Execution**
AWS Transfer Family Managed Workflows (for SFTP channels) and S3 Event Notifications (for direct PUT and API Gateway channels) trigger a scan Lambda function on each file arrival. The Lambda function scans the object, returns a structured result, and tags the object (`scan-status: CLEAN / INFECTED / ERROR`, `scan-engine-version`, `scan-definition-version`, `scan-timestamp`).

**Layer 3 — Outcome Routing**
A promotion gate checks the `scan-status` tag. `CLEAN` objects are copied to the destination store and removed from staging. `INFECTED` and `ERROR` objects are moved to a quarantine bucket (deny-all-except-SOC access policy; dedicated KMS key; retains PHI data classification of the source channel). No object reaches a destination store without a confirmed `CLEAN` tag.

**Layer 4 — Alerting, Logging, and Definition Currency**
`INFECTED` outcomes publish a structured event to EventBridge → SNS → SOC/SIEM integration. All scan outcomes are logged to an immutable CloudWatch log group. An EventBridge Scheduler rule fires daily, triggering CodeBuild to rebuild the scan engine container image with the latest definitions and publish to ECR; the Lambda function is updated to reference the new image. Staleness monitoring alerts Platform Engineering at 24-hour and SOC at 48-hour definition lag thresholds.

### Implementation Type

- [ ] **Single Tenant** — Dedicated instance per customer
- [x] **Multi-Tenant** — Shared platform scanning service across all ingest channels

**Justification**: The staging infrastructure, ClamAV Lambda function, ECR registry, CodeBuild definition pipeline, quarantine store, and SOC alerting chain are platform-level shared services. [governance/crb-submissions/pg-inbound-file-scanning-service-crb.md#strategic-alignment]

### Strategic Alignment

This capability directly advances Platform Gainwell's security posture objective to close the malicious code protection gap identified in the Cloud and Infrastructure Security capability model. It is a prerequisite for achieving NIST 800-53 SI-3 architectural intent at the platform layer and for meeting HIPAA §164.308(a)(1) requirements for protection from malicious software across all systems that handle PHI.

The capability is fully aligned with the Zero Trust principle of explicit verification — no inbound file is trusted based on the source channel or submitting identity alone; every file is independently verified at the data boundary before access to a protected store is permitted.

The architecture pattern is engine-agnostic by design (ABB GUID-SEC-CLOUD-FILE-SCAN-2.6.11 and RAD GUID-SEC-CLOUD-FILE-SCAN-RAD-3.6.04 are vendor-neutral). Scan engine selection is governed by ADR-SEC-003-FILE-SCAN, currently under Security Architecture review, and does not affect the conceptual approval of this capability. Any engine selected from the ADR evaluation will fit within the surrounding platform pattern without re-architecture.

**AI/ML Integration**: No AI/ML components in this capability. The scan engine (ClamAV) uses signature-based and limited heuristic detection — not machine learning inference.

[governance/crb-submissions/pg-inbound-file-scanning-service-crb.md#security-considerations]

### Security Considerations

- **PII/PHI Handling**: Files transiting the scanning service may contain PHI. The staging store, quarantine store, and audit log must all inherit the data classification of the highest-classified ingest channel they serve. KMS customer-managed keys (CMKs) with PHI-restricted key policies must be used for all scan tiers serving PHI-classified channels. Infected PHI objects in the quarantine store are subject to HIPAA retention and legal hold requirements — destruction requires documented authorization.
- **Access Control**: The scan engine Lambda execution role holds read access to the staging bucket only. The promotion role holds write access to the destination bucket. The quarantine store uses a deny-all-except-SOC bucket policy. No identity outside the scan workflow holds write access to any destination store. IAM policies are codified in the IaC Terraform formation and subject to automated drift detection.
- **Encryption**: All staging, destination, and quarantine stores use KMS encryption with distinct keys per classification tier. Quarantine store key access is restricted to Security Operations roles only. Key rotation follows the enterprise KMS governance policy (GUID-SEC-DATA-KMS-2.5.04).
- **Audit Logging**: All scan events (CLEAN and INFECTED) are logged to an immutable CloudWatch log group with a retention policy aligned to HIPAA retention requirements. Log fields include: object key, source channel, scan result, threat name, engine version, definition version, and timestamp. Logs are protected from modification by IAM policy (AU-9).
- **Privacy Impact**: The scan service processes file content but does not retain it beyond the scan execution window. The audit log retains scan metadata (not file content). The quarantine store retains infected file content under Security Operations custody. No additional Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) is required beyond the existing PHI handling controls for the ingest channels served, provided the quarantine store is governed under the same HIPAA-scoped access controls as the source channels.
- **SOC Integration**: Alert events contain structured metadata (object key, source channel, threat name, uploader identity, timestamp, quarantine reference) — no raw file content is transmitted in the alert payload. SIEM ingest of alert events follows the enterprise monitoring integration pattern (GUID-SEC-SECOPS-MON-2.1.01).
page_texts.25:
[governance/crb-submissions/pg-inbound-file-scanning-service-crb.md#non-functional-requirements]

### Non-Functional Requirements

- **Performance**: Scan latency per file must not materially degrade ingest SLAs for in-scope channels. Lambda scan time for the baseline evaluation option is benchmarked at <5 seconds for files up to 50MB (AWS Solutions Library reference; actual performance will be validated against the engine selected via ADR-SEC-003-FILE-SCAN); larger files require dedicated large-file scan path sizing. Lambda provisioned concurrency must be configured for Transfer Family channels with SLA commitments.
- **Scalability**: Serverless scan engine (Lambda) scales with concurrent file ingest events. Lambda reserved concurrency must be sized per channel throughput profile. S3, ECR, and CodeBuild are regionally scalable with no manual capacity management.
- **Availability**: The scan service is in the critical path of all ingest workflows. Fail-closed posture means unavailability blocks ingest — this is intentional and acceptable per the ABB. Platform Engineering must document the operational runbook for scan service outage scenarios, including the escalation path for business-critical ingest channels.
- **Reliability**: The definition update pipeline must be monitored and must not leave the scan engine operating with a partially updated definition set. Prior image version is retained as an active fallback.
- **Maintainability**: All infrastructure is codified as Terraform in `iac/terraform/formations/aws/`. The scan engine container image is managed through the CodeBuild pipeline. No manual configuration steps after initial deployment.
- **Compatibility**: ClamAV on Lambda is compatible with all three v1 ingest channel patterns (Transfer Family Managed Workflow invocation, S3 Event Notification Lambda trigger, API Gateway Lambda integration). The scan engine container image runs on the Lambda container image runtime (Amazon Linux 2023 base).

### Vendor / Partner Evaluation

**Technology Decisions**

> **Note**: Scan engine selection is out of scope for this CRB and is governed by ADR-SEC-003-FILE-SCAN, currently under Security Architecture review. The table below covers platform-layer infrastructure decisions only.

| Technology Category | Selected | Alternatives Considered | Decision Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Workflow orchestration (SFTP channel) | AWS Transfer Family Managed Workflows | Custom Lambda orchestration, Step Functions | Native Transfer Family integration; no additional orchestration service required; managed workflow is the AWS-recommended pattern for the SFTP ingest scenario |
| Workflow orchestration (S3/API channel) | S3 Event Notification → Lambda | EventBridge Pipes, Step Functions | Lowest-latency trigger path for S3 object creation; no intermediate routing service required for simple trigger-scan-tag pattern |
| Definition update pipeline | EventBridge Scheduler → CodeBuild → ECR | Manual update, SSM Automation | Fully automated, auditable, and observable; EventBridge cron scheduling with CodeBuild provides a proven AWS-native CI/CD pipeline pattern for container image updates |
| Container registry | Amazon ECR | DockerHub, GitHub Container Registry | ECR is the enterprise-standard container registry on AWS; VPC endpoint available for Lambda pull without public internet egress |

**Licensing**

> **Note**: Scan engine licensing is subject to the ADR-SEC-003-FILE-SCAN outcome and will be confirmed after ADR ratification.

| Technology | License | Annual Cost | Compliance Requirements |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AWS Transfer Family | AWS commercial | Consumption-based per enterprise AWS agreement | Governed by existing AWS EA; Managed Workflows priced per workflow execution and per GB processed |
| AWS Lambda | AWS commercial | Consumption-based | $0.20 per 1M requests at current volumes |
| Amazon ECR | AWS commercial | ~$12/month for ClamAV image storage (per AWS Solutions Library estimate) | Standard ECR pricing per GB stored |
| AWS CodeBuild | AWS commercial | ~$0.54/month at 3,000 build requests (per AWS Solutions Library estimate) | Standard CodeBuild pricing per build minute |
